question: Should OpenClaw accept this default-off core continuation substrate with cross-session delegate routing, trusted internal system events, and new config/protocol/state surfaces?
rationale: The remaining blocker is not a small code repair: maintainers must decide whether this broad core contract is the right product boundary and whether the security/session-state tradeoffs are acceptable after exact-head proof.

options.title: Approve after proof and security review
options.body: Require a branch refresh, exact-head accepted-compaction proof, upgrade proof for SQLite/config/protocol surfaces, and explicit security/product approval before merge.

options.title: Split to a narrower substrate
options.body: Land a smaller same-session/default-off continuation slice first and defer cross-session targeting, request_compaction, and broader SDK/protocol exposure.

options.title: Pause core continuation
options.body: Keep the experimentation external or close the PR if maintainers decide continuation should not become an OpenClaw core contract now.

recommendation.title: Approve after proof and security review
recommendation.body: Require a branch refresh, exact-head accepted-compaction proof, upgrade proof for SQLite/config/protocol surfaces, and explicit security/product approval before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest recent history across the central agent runner, tool assembly, TaskFlow, and system-event boundaries affected by this PR.
